coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay Kids' Park
record.summary: A playground at Long Bridge and China Basin streets in Mission Bay, part of the Mission Bay Parks system (labeled P6 on OCII's current Mission Bay South open-space page), that opened to the public in 2016 after months of delay; the exact day is inconsistently reported across the two sources found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon tagged with the Mission Bay Parks system's own URL for this facility, at Long Bridge St & China Basin St.

facts.value: P6 ("Kids Park"), per OCII's current Mission Bay South open-space page

milestones.text: Playground construction visibly complete (grass grown in, play equipment and nature huts installed) per contemporaneous local reporting, but not yet open to the public pending a land-transfer procedure and street work

open_questions: Exact opening date is unresolved: the Urban Life Signs blog post says the playground opened Friday, July 1, 2016; Mission Bay Parks' own post announcing the opening is dated September 15, 2016 and doesn't state a specific day, raising the possibility of a later or phased opening than the blog's July date -- flagged rather than picked.
Neither source names a designer, landscape architect or general contractor.

The 2015 under-construction/visibly-finished date is derived from the Urban Life Signs post (published June 2016), which describes the playground as having looked complete, with grass grown in, 'over a year ago' -- an approximate back-calculation, not a directly stated date. A separate SFist article (May 26, 2016, 'Completed Mission Bay Park Fenced Off For Months Due To Red Tape') and an SF Chronicle article (June 12, 2016) both corroborate that construction was finished well before the delayed opening, describing it as fenced off for 'months' after being 'finished in March,' but neither independently confirms 2015 versus early 2016; 2015 is used here as the more specific of the two estimates but is flagged as approximate.
